A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GF-NODE, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Retained material can be matched: v2 Appendices B and C become v3 Appendices E and B, respectively.

before.justification: v2 reports original trajectory-prediction results on MD17 and alanine dipeptide, structural evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those results and reports additional revised-MD17 and larger-system experiments, extended forecasts, spatial-temporal correlations, and structural and timing analyses.

M1.justification: The GNN encoder, GFT, scalar/vector spectral ODEs with mode attention, inverse GFT, decoder, and position-MSE objective are retained. Appendix A.3 explicitly documents the existing loss, while the new equivariance discussion does not establish an implemented architectural change.

E1.justification: v3 retains original MD17 and alanine evaluations and adds nine revised-MD17 molecules, including Azobenzene and Paracetamol. It also evaluates Ac-Ala3-NHMe, AT-AT-CG-CG, Bucky-Catcher, and a double-walled nanotube from MD22, substantially extending molecular size and physical-system coverage. Ala2 corresponds to the retained alanine case.

E2.justification: The five MD17 comparators remain NDCN, LG-ODE, EGNN, EGNO, and ITO. However, v3 Table 13 additionally reports LG-ODE in the Ala2 comparison, whereas v2 Table 3 compares alanine against only NDCN, ITO, EGNO, and EGNN.

E3.justification: The original splits, eight-frame sampling, and 3000-step training horizon remain. v3 adds 10000-step evaluations, forecasting curves through 15000 steps, and spatial-temporal, RDF, and timing evaluation procedures. Appendix A.1 also changes the stated MD17 simulation duration from 200 to 2000 ps; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing component, backbone, and embedding ablations are retained. v3 adds direct spatial-temporal correspondence analysis, extended stability tests, larger-system component ablations at 10000 steps, runtime sensitivity to mode count, and system-averaged and element-specific RDF analyses (Figures 9–17). These test substantial additional mechanism, scalability, and structural-fidelity questions.

E5.justification: Figure 12 newly specifies three repeated timing runs at each mode count and error bars representing their variability. Existing accuracy tables retain their previous plus/minus reporting; v3 does not newly specify accuracy-run counts, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain identical numerical entries. Tables 11–14 and Figures 9–17 add substantial benchmark, forecasting, correlation, structural, ablation, and timing results. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v2. The new tables include exceptions to universal superiority: EGNO has lower mean MSE than GF-NODE for Malonaldehyde at 3000 steps (37.90 versus 37.92) and Paracetamol at 10000 steps (27.12 versus 27.20).

T1.justification: v3 adds heat-equation mode dynamics in Proposition 3.3 and Appendix C, formal definitions for joint spatial-temporal analysis with a local-stationarity assumption, and an SO(3)-equivariance theorem with module-level arguments in Appendix D. The earlier spectral-decomposition and truncation results are retained in Appendix B.

C1.justification: Beyond v2's architecture and prediction claims, v3 presents theoretical foundations and formal equivariance guarantees as contributions. Its introduction and conclusion broaden the performance claim to larger systems and horizons through 15000 steps, including best performance across all evaluated cases. That universal wording exceeds what Tables 11 and 12 support.

C2.justification: Section 4.7 and Appendix C newly interpret spatial-temporal correlations as support for a dynamical frequency hierarchy and low-frequency truncation. They attribute weaker Bucky-Catcher correlation to structural complexity and qualify the heat-equation model as simplified. Appendix F adds interpretations of RDF agreement as preservation of local and intermediate-range structure.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit formula for the existing MSE loss, centering/projection/PSD instructions for the new analysis, MDShare source attribution, molecular atom counts, and NVIDIA L40 GPU/AMD Ryzen 9 7950X CPU timing hardware. The principal training hyperparameters, solver settings, and public code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Christensen and von Lilienfeld (2020) and Chmiela et al. (2023) for the additional datasets. Appendix D explicitly relates its proof presentation to EGNO. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against neural operators and Graph Neural ODEs are otherwise largely retained.

P1.justification: Most original explanatory and related-work prose remains. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion are expanded, RQ4 and acknowledgements are added, and appendices are reorganized around the new material. These are localized narrative revisions rather than an extensive rewrite of the retained paper.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 11–15 and Figures 9–17, substantially expanding the visual presentation with correlation plots, forecasting panels, timing curves, ablations, and RDFs. Existing graphics are retained and relocated, with Figures 1 and 2 exchanging numbering. Journal headers and expanded author affiliations also change the opening layout.

improvement.justification: The larger-system tests, longer forecasts, and structural diagnostics improve the empirical support beyond v2's narrower evaluation. The net gain is tempered by new overclaims: Tables 11–12 contradict universal best performance, and Appendix D assumes EGNN backbones while asserting rotation commutation for MLP-based ODEs without sufficient justification. Thus the empirical evidence improves, but the stronger formal guarantees remain inadequately supported.
